title: Random forests trained offline in Python, run in the browser
context: train_synth.py fits scikit-learn RandomForestClassifier (validity) and one RandomForestRegressor per output metric (150 trees, max_depth 15, min_samples_leaf 2), serializes every tree to JSON, and 11-forest.js walks them in the browser. Tree spread doubles as the confidence signal (12-search-core.js scoreCandidate).

options.name: Random forests (current)
options.summary: Per-metric RF regressors plus an RF validity classifier, exported as raw trees.
pros: Beat an MLP by 0.5+ mean R² at 257 samples (README)
Tree disagreement gives a free confidence signal
Exact parity between Python and JS (tests/forest-parity.js)
cons: Big bundle: 1,650 trees of depth up to 15
Cannot extrapolate past the training range
Piecewise-constant predictions give the search flat regions

options.name: Gradient-boosted trees
options.summary: LightGBM or XGBoost, still exported as trees and walked by the same packed-node code.
pros: Usually better R² per byte; far fewer, shallower trees
cons: Loses tree spread as a confidence signal; would need quantile heads or an ensemble

options.name: Small neural net via ONNX or hand-written inference
options.summary: An MLP once Vault has enough rows.
cons: Lost to RF at small data sizes; still only ~2.5k rows

recommendation: README "Random Forest, not MLP" records the empirical comparison; train_synth.py and 11-forest.js are built around it, and the confidence signal (12-search-core.js) depends on per-tree spread.
